title: The affine-local function-field square is a pullback of the diagonal
statement: Let X be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], η its generic point [def-sc-generic-point], U a nonempty affine open, and x a point outside U whose local ring B = O_{X,x} [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is Noetherian of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put A = Γ(X,U), K = k(X) [def-sc-function-field], and T = A ⊗_ℤ B. Let φ : T → K be the canonical map induced by the germ map A → K and the stalk-specialization map B → K. Let j_A : Spec A → X be the affine-open chart, j_B : Spec B → X the canonical local-scheme morphism, and c : Spec K → X the canonical generic-stalk morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let q : Spec T → X × X be the pair of the spectrum maps of the tensor inclusions followed by j_A and j_B. Then the square with top arrow c, left arrow Spec φ, right arrow the diagonal X → X × X, and bottom arrow q is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. No separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Varieties Lemma Tag 09NB, opening paragraph of its proof; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09NB

proof.text: The stalk B is a local domain with fraction field K by lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field. The canonical morphism Spec B → X identifies points with generalizations of x and induces stalk isomorphisms by lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism. Its inverse image of U omits the closed point and contains the generic point. A one-dimensional local domain has no other primes: a nonzero prime properly below its maximal ideal would make a prime chain of length two.

Choose a nonzero element t in the maximal ideal of B; it exists because a field has dimension zero. The inverse image of U is D(t), with coordinate ring B[1/t] by lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion and lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change. Its canonical map to K is an isomorphism by lem-sc-local-domain-dim-one-principal-localization-fraction-field. Consequently the two canonical maps Spec K → Spec A and Spec K → Spec B exhibit Spec K as Spec A ×_X Spec B. Their composite to X is the map from its generic stalk.

Identify the product Spec A × Spec B with Spec (A ⊗_ℤ B) by the affine-spectrum tensor-product description (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra), applied to the terminal integer spectrum (with a universe lift if needed). The two projections are spectra of the tensor inclusions. Composing the spectrum of the tensor lift with these projections gives respectively the germ map A → K and the canonical stalk map B → K, by the defining equations of the lift.

For any arrows Y → X and Z → X, the fibre product Y ×_X Z is the pullback of X → X × X along Y × Z → X × X: a cone to this square is exactly a pair of maps to Y and Z whose composites to X agree, with that common composite as the map to X. Apply this universal property to the preceding identifications; it gives the displayed IsPullback square and uses no separatedness.

theorem Scheme.isPullback_affine_local_functionField_diagonal
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) [Nonempty U]
    (x : X) (hx : x ∉ U)
    [IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1) :
    let A : Type u := Γ(X, U)
    let B : Type u := X.presheaf.stalk x
    let K : Type u := X.functionField
    let φ : TensorProduct ℤ A B →ₐ[ℤ] K :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.lift
        (X.germToFunctionField U).hom.toIntAlgHom
        (algebraMap B K).toIntAlgHom
        (fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _)
    IsPullback (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom))
      (prod.lift (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X))
      (prod.lift
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom : A →+* TensorProduct ℤ A B)) ≫
          hU.fromSpec)
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom : B →+* TensorProduct ℤ A B)) ≫
          X.fromSpecStalk x))
